gen.title: From Limited Offer to Wider Divides
gen.orderNote: Trace the cause and effect chain as the text unfolds from negotiation to aftermath.

steps.label: authorized to pay France up to $10 million
steps.quote: negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe were authorized to pay France up to $10 million solely for the port of New Orleans

steps.label: offered the entire territory of Louisiana
steps.quote: when they were offered the entire territory of Louisiana – an area larger than Great Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal combined

steps.label: strict interpreter of the Constitution
steps.quote: President Thomas Jefferson was generally a strict interpreter of the Constitution who wondered if the U.S. Government

steps.label: Jefferson squelched whatever doubts he had
steps.quote: As Napoleon threatened to take back the offer, Jefferson squelched whatever doubts he had and prepared to occupy a land of unimaginable riches.

steps.label: first major cession of land
steps.quote: The Louisiana Purchase was the first major cession of land in a long series of expansions that span the 19th century.

steps.label: sectional weaknesses between the North and South
steps.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery
